transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, thanks. I guess what brings me in is that my eating has gotten pretty out of hand lately. After my late shifts, I’ll stop for takeout on the way home and end up eating... well, like two burgers, fries, a shake. But then I still go home and just clean out the leftovers in the garage fridge. It’s like it’s a whole second supper. I just need to figure out how to get a handle on it.
After these episodes, do you do anything to try to make up for the food you've eaten?

No, I don't. I mean, if you're asking if I make myself throw up or take pills or something... no, nothing like that. I don't go run ten miles or anything either. 

Usually, I just feel pretty miserable and stuffed, and then I just go to sleep. I wake up the next day and just go about my normal routine, honestly. I don't really do anything to work it off.
During these times when you're eating, do you feel like you can't stop, or that you've lost control over how much you're eating?

Yeah, that's exactly what it feels like. Once I start eating, it's like a switch is flipped. I'll actually be sitting there telling myself, "Roy, shut the bag and just go inside," but I can't do it. My hands just keep reaching for more food, and I just keep eating even though I know I should stop. It definitely feels like I've completely lost control.
On average, how many times a week do these episodes happen?

Well, for the past few months, it's been happening at least once a week. But honestly, it's often more like two or three times. It usually hits me after a late shift or if I've had a particularly rough day on the line.
